narrative.overview:
The app reads like a Federal Register or CFR page set for a working desk: a GPO-navy rail on the left, a cool off-white ground, white work surfaces, and black hairline rules that do the job cards usually do. Every number on screen sits next to the record it came from, and those records can be opened. Structure comes from rules, weight and alignment, not from boxes, tints or shadows. The pages are dense and calm. Hierarchy is set with three type sizes plus one display figure, the facility's probability.

Colour carries meaning, not decoration. Navy is the institution (rail, sign-in panel, the one filled button). Citation blue is anything you can follow. Oxblood is risk and G to L severity only. Amber is a state that needs attention. Pale yellow is a record the reader has marked. Everything else is ink, grey and rule.

The world rejects the KPI-card dashboard and the chatbot pane. Tables, definition lists, fixed-scale bars and the 36-month citation strip are the main forms.
keyCharacteristics: Navy rail (232px) plus a white freshness line (month, model, scored date, data flags) above every page.
Hairline rules as structure: an ink rule under section titles and table heads, soft rules between rows.
Tabular figures everywhere, and one identifier notation (Roboto Mono) for CCNs, evidence IDs and run IDs.
Fixed scales: a 10-step decile meter, a 0-to-1 probability scale and a 36-month axis that read the same on every facility.
A marked record holds its pale-yellow mark until the reader dismisses it.

rules.name: The Oxblood Means Risk Rule
rules.body: Oxblood is used only for the model's risk and G to L severity. A heading, a button or an error is never oxblood.

rules.name: The Blue Is a Link Rule
rules.body: Citation blue marks only something you can follow or activate: a link, a chip, a text button, the focus ring. Never decoration.

rules.name: The Decile Ramp Rule
rules.body: Decile colour mixes oxblood into paper in OKLCH, 100% for the riskiest tenth down to 10% (never below 8%). The same ramp is used on every screen.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: The app runs on 0.8125rem, 0.875rem and 1.5rem. Rank comes from weight (400/600/700), colour (ink or muted) and a rule. The display figure is the only exception.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the body and never turned off, so columns of numbers line up.

rules.name: The One Notation Rule
rules.body: An identifier is always mono, and evidence IDs wrap only after their colons.

rules.name: The Rules, Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Sections are separated by an ink rule under their title and by whitespace, not by bordered or shadowed containers. Borders are kept for controls, panels for error and empty states, and the mark.

dos: Do show the data month, model version and caveat next to every score: the freshness line on every page, and the "About this score" block on the facility.
Do attach an evidence chip or a record anchor to every claim, so the citation rail can resolve it.
Do separate sections with an ink rule under a bold 0.875rem title, and table rows with soft rules.
Do keep the decile meter, the 0-to-1 bars and the 36-month axis fixed, so any two facilities compare at a glance.
Do pair every colour signal with text: severity letters, decile labels, bar values as text, flag wording.
Do set every identifier in Roboto Mono.
donts: Don't use oxblood for anything but model risk and G to L severity.
Don't build pages from KPI cards or shadowed containers. Rules and whitespace carry the structure.
Don't add a fourth UI type size. Rank comes from weight, colour and rule.
Don't let a mark clear on blur or hover-out. It holds until the reader dismisses it.
Don't set agent prose or regulation quotes in Public Sans once they ship. Merriweather is reserved for them, and only for them.
Don't use amber for decoration. It is only for states that need attention.
